open_questions.q: Should the initial built-in Microsoft ID catalog include well-known first-party application IDs?
open_questions.assumed: No. Initial scope includes Entra built-in directory role templates and the three built-in authentication strength policies; first-party application IDs are deferred.

open_questions.q: Should built-in Entra directory-role and authentication-strength IDs resolve only with --resolve-all-guids, or by default in attributes whose semantic type is already recognized?
open_questions.assumed: Resolve them by default in recognized semantic attributes; require --resolve-all-guids when they occur in arbitrary or free-form attributes.

open_questions.q: How should a GUID that appears in multiple mapping sources be resolved?
open_questions.assumed: A user-provided mapping overrides an offline built-in catalog entry; among existing user mapping sections, preserve the product's established precedence and entity-specific formatting rather than inventing a new order.

open_questions.q: When broad resolution has no semantic context and the same GUID appears in more than one user mapping section, which label and entity type should be shown?
open_questions.assumed: Leave the GUID raw because the match is ambiguous. When semantic context is known, use only its matching category; when exactly one user mapping matches, it overrides an offline built-in name.
